title: Nine Days Gone
subtitle: A Studio Portrait, a Locker at Union Station, a Room Above the Carousel

setting.name: Los Angeles, Monday 22 to Wednesday 24 September 1947
setting.description: Two and a half days of late-summer heat. The party starts on the Castellane lot in Hollywood, where Harlan Shay hires them and where Vivian Lark's dressing bungalow and the transport garage hold the first clues; follows her trail downtown to Union Station and up Angels Flight to a Bunker Hill rooming house where she lived as Dot Pell; pays a call on her friend the screenwriter Abel Kurland in Laurel Canyon, who lies to them kindly; may brush against Club Sirocco on the Strip, whose owner wants her even more than the studio does; and ends at the Santa Monica pier in the fog, in a room above the carousel, with Royce Ambler's men coming up the stairs. Vivian is not lost. She is hiding, and she has very good reasons. The scenario's last scene is a swimming pool in Laurel Canyon at dawn.
setting.atmosphere: Heat shimmer on Santa Monica Boulevard, the studio's white walls too bright to look at, the cool of Union Station's tiled waiting room, the creak and clank of Angels Flight, cabbage and floor polish in a rooming-house hallway, the calliope music of the Santa Monica carousel and the foghorn under it. Everyone the party meets has an opinion about Vivian, and none of them are the same girl: the studio's 'good kid from a small town', the landlady's 'Dot who pays on time', the screenwriter's 'the best natural actress on the lot', the club owner's 'a thief'. Let the players assemble her from the pieces. Most of this scenario is legwork and conversation; violence comes once, at the end, on the pier.

keyLocations.name: Castellane Pictures: Shay's Bungalow, Vivian's Dressing Bungalow, the Transport Garage
keyLocations.description: The studio's two walled blocks on Santa Monica Boulevard. Harlan Shay works from an unmarked white bungalow behind the commissary with a lemon tree, a secretary called Miss Abernathy and three telephones. Vivian's dressing bungalow is one of a row of small stucco cottages for featured players, with her name painted on a board that can be changed in an afternoon. The transport garage, by the Gower Street gate, holds the studio's fleet of limousines and station wagons and a dispatcher's window with a log book.
features: Vivian's bungalow: a dressing table, a daybed, a rack of studio wardrobe, a wastebasket nobody has emptied because Shay told the cleaners to leave it alone
The transport dispatcher's log, a ledger with every car out and in, driver, time and destination
The studio personnel office, where contract players' legal names, addresses and next of kin are on file cards
Studio police on bicycles who answer to Shay, and a commissary where everyone gossips
encounters: Harlan Shay's briefing: coffee, $500 in fifties, a portrait, and a story about a small-town girl and a man
Miss Abernathy, Shay's secretary, fifty, devoted to him, who will say only that Mr. Shay has not slept properly in a week
Agnes Whitlow, the script supervisor on The Gilded Hour, who liked Vivian and does not like being lied to (companion)
secrets: CLUE C1a (core, Investigation or simply looking): the bungalow has been left as if Vivian expects never to come back. The things a person takes when they leave on purpose are gone: her makeup case, her mother's photograph from the mirror frame, her own two cotton dresses. The studio's things are all still here, down to a borrowed mink stole, carefully hung. A kidnapped woman does not pack; a woman running off with a man does not leave the mink.

CLUE C2b (core): in the wastebasket, torn in two, a picture postcard of Angels Flight: 'Dot, your old room is always here if the pictures ever get too much. Rent is still seven dollars. G. Sloane, Alta Vista Rooms, Clay Street.' Postmarked July.
CLUE C1b (core): the dispatcher's log for Sunday 14 September: 'Car 11, Shearer, out 9:15 p.m., Union Sta., in 10:30 p.m.' If Bunny Shearer is a player character, her player already knows why.

CLUE C2a (core): Vivian's personnel card: legal name Dorothy Ann Pell, born Taft, Calif., 1923; next of kin a mother, deceased; previous address 'Alta Vista Rooms, Clay St., L.A.' A dollar to the personnel clerk, or Percy Ainsworth's say-so as her agent, opens the drawer.

Also in the wastebasket, Investigation DC 13: a Club Sirocco matchbook with '4-17' pencilled inside the flap. (It is the first half of Ambler's safe combination, written down once while she learned it, and it means nothing yet.)

keyLocations.name: Union Station
keyLocations.description: Eight years old and the finest building in Los Angeles: a Mission-style tower, a waiting room with a ceiling of painted beams, leather armchairs and tiled floors in patterns like a Spanish carpet, two gardens, a long restaurant counter, a newsstand, redcaps in their caps, and a long bank of coin lockers by the ticket concourse.
features: The ticket windows, where a clerk keeps the stubs of the week's sales
The lockers: locker 212 has a 24-hour coin slot that someone has kept paying by the week through the station's left-luggage office
The redcaps' bench by the north patio, where the same six men see everyone
The streetcar stop on Alameda Street outside, and the Red Car terminal next door
encounters: Clarence Webb, redcap, sixty, who remembers Vivian because she tipped him a dollar to carry a suitcase twenty yards and then asked him which streetcar went to Hill Street
A Pickpocket working the waiting room, who lifts something from the least careful party member and can be caught (Perception DC 13) and turned into a source for a dollar
A Beat Cop who does not like people forcing lockers
secrets: CLUE C1c (core): the ticket clerk's book shows one coach ticket to Bakersfield on the Sunday-night train sold to 'Miss V. Lark' at 9:52 p.m.; the conductor's lifted-ticket count for that train came back one short. She bought a ticket and did not get on. Clarence Webb saw her walk out to the Alameda Street streetcars without her suitcase.

CLUE C2c (core): the left-luggage office has locker 212 paid by the week in the name 'D. Pell', in cash, by a young woman in a headscarf. Inside (Bunny's claim check, a $5 bribe, or Sleight of Hand DC 15 and +1 Heat if seen): a suitcase holding a white fox fur, a paste necklace from the studio jewelry department and two studio gowns. It is a false trail meant for the studio, and a message: she is giving them back.
Clarence Webb, for a dollar and courtesy: 'She asked me the car for Hill Street and Angels Flight. Pretty girl. Nervous. Looked behind her like she owed somebody money.'

keyLocations.name: Bunker Hill: Angels Flight and the Alta Vista Rooms
keyLocations.description: A crumbling Victorian mansion on Clay Street with a turret, a porch that sags and fourteen rooms let by the week to pensioners, a night-shift waitress, a retired trombonist and whoever else comes up the hill. Mrs. Gertrude 'Gertie' Sloane, seventy, runs it from a parlour full of ferns and photographs of her late husband. Angels Flight's two little cars, Sinai and Olivet, haul passengers up the slope from Hill Street for a penny.
features: Room 9 on the second floor, Vivian's room, paid to the end of the month; the bed made, the closet nearly empty
A shared bathroom at the end of the hall and a back stair to the alley
The Angels Flight station house at the top, where the operator sits in his booth and sees everyone who rides
The view: downtown, the City Hall tower, and on clear nights the searchlights over Hollywood
encounters: Mrs. Sloane, with a bruise on her cheekbone and a broken teacup she has glued, who will say nothing at all to anyone who looks like Tiny Bascombe and everything to anyone who is kind
Mr. Albert Dunphy, the Angels Flight operator, who has a memory for faces and a dime-store novel in his lap
If the party is slow (they arrive after Tuesday noon): two Street Toughs from the Sirocco, back for a second look
secrets: CLUE C3a (core): on Saturday 20 September a very large man in a camel overcoat, too warm for the weather, with a Club Sirocco doorman's pin on his lapel, came asking for 'Miss Lark, or Dot, whatever she calls herself now'. When Mrs. Sloane said she had no Miss Lark he knocked the teacup out of her hand, and her face hit the door frame. Dot left that night.

CLUE C2d (core): Albert Dunphy at Angels Flight: 'Dot? Every morning about eight that week, headscarf and dark glasses, down to Hill Street, back up at six with a paper sack of groceries. Rode with me Saturday night with a suitcase, last car, about ten. Didn't come back.'

CLUE C4a (core, searching room 9): tucked into the mirror frame and forgotten, a strip of four penny-arcade photographs, Vivian and a white-haired old woman with enormous eyes pulling faces, stamped on the back 'PLAYLAND ARCADE, SANTA MONICA PIER'. Mrs. Sloane knows the old woman: 'That's Mags. Marguerite Fennimore. She was in pictures before they talked. Dot boarded with her when she first came to town. Mags lives out at the beach now, over the merry-go-round.'
Mrs. Sloane's last word, if the party is gentle: 'She said to tell anyone kind that she's all right and she'll pay me back. She said to tell anyone else nothing.'

keyLocations.name: Abel Kurland's House, Laurel Canyon
keyLocations.description: A shingled house on a steep lot off Lookout Mountain Avenue, too much house for a writer between contracts, with a study full of books and a Royal typewriter, a living room with a wall of glass, a flagstone terrace and a small kidney-shaped pool lit from underneath. Kurland lives alone since his divorce. A maid, Lupe Ortega, comes three mornings a week.
features: The study: the typewriter, the script of Dry Wells in a stack, a telephone with the number of the Hollywood answering service taped to it
The pool and its flagstone deck, the concrete coping, a diving board at the deep end
A wet bar with a single good bottle of gin
Neighbours close enough on the hillside to hear an argument
encounters: Abel Kurland, on Tuesday afternoon, in shirtsleeves with a pencil behind his ear and a committee subpoena unopened on his desk, who is charming, funny, frightened, and lies to protect Vivian
If the party visits on Tuesday afternoon: Tiny Bascombe's Buick parked a hundred yards down the road, and Tiny asking Lupe Ortega whether Miss Lark has been visiting
secrets: CLUE C3b (core, Insight or just watching him): Kurland goes still when Club Sirocco is mentioned. Pinned to his corkboard among index cards for Dry Wells is a Sirocco card-room menu with five sets of initials pencilled on the back, two of them D.H. and R.F. If asked about it he says it's 'research' and changes the subject. Insight DC 13: he is not afraid for himself; he is afraid for her.

CLUE C4b (core, if the party asks about calls or charms the operator by telephone): his answering service, Hollywood Personal Answering Service, logged a call on Sunday 21 September from 'Miss Pell' on a Santa Monica exchange, SAnta Monica 4-1180, which the reverse directory at any newspaper or the phone company lists as the Hippodrome Building, Santa Monica Pier.

Kurland will say, if the party is honest about who hired them: 'Then you work for Harlan, and Harlan works for Bernard, and Bernard works for anyone with a check. Go home. Tell Harlan she's in Mexico.' Anything the party tells Shay about this conversation, Shay acts on that night (see the campaign's Nightly Report rule). This is the visit that kills Abel Kurland, whether or not the party ever knows it.

keyLocations.name: Club Sirocco, the Sunset Strip
keyLocations.description: Royce Ambler's nightclub on the county side of Sunset: white Moorish arches, a palm court with a fountain, a twelve-piece band, a dance floor under a ceiling painted like a desert night, and upstairs a card room nobody admits exists. In this scenario the party sees only the ground floor, by day or early evening; the card room is for kl-scenario-003.
features: The hat-check alcove and its girl, Dolores 'Dee Dee' Carmody, who sees everyone arrive and leave
Tiny Bascombe on the door in a camel overcoat
The kitchen door to the alley, the service stair, and Ambler's office above the bandstand
encounters: Royce Ambler himself, if the party asks for him by name: courteous, Kansas City accent, offers a drink, says Miss Lark is a dear friend of the club and he too is worried about her, and asks a little too casually whether she 'left anything with anyone'
Tiny Bascombe and a Bouncer, who escort the party out if they push
secrets: CLUE C3d (core, a dollar and a kind word to Dee Dee, or Persuasion DC 10 for more detail): 'Saturday the thirteenth she came in with the studio party, went upstairs, came down white as a sheet twenty minutes later and went out through the kitchen with her purse held like a football. Next morning Mr. Ambler had the safe man in from Glendale, and he's had Tiny looking for her ever since.'
Ambler's question, 'did she leave anything with anyone', is also a clue, and Insight DC 12 reads it: he does not care where she is, he cares what she has.

keyLocations.name: The Santa Monica Pier and the Hippodrome
keyLocations.description: The long wooden pier at the end of Colorado Avenue, with bait shops, a café, the Playland arcade and its photo booth, fortune-telling machines, fishing lines over the rail, and the big Moorish-style hippodrome that houses the carousel: forty-four hand-carved horses going round under a ceiling of lights, a band organ, and upstairs a row of small apartments with windows over the sea. Mags Fennimore has the corner one. At night the fog comes in and the foghorn sounds.
features: The carousel floor: horses, brass poles, mirrors, the band organ's drums and pipes, and the operator's booth
An outside stair and an inside stair to the apartments, and a catwalk along the windows
The pier's planks, the rail, the drop of thirty feet into black water, and the pilings beneath
The fog, which cuts sight to twenty feet and gives advantage on Stealth to anyone who knows the pier
encounters: Mags Fennimore, seventy-two, silent-picture actress, who meets the party at her door with a carving knife and stage presence
Vivian Lark (companion, full sheet), who has been waiting for someone to find her and has decided what she will say
Tiny Bascombe, two Street Toughs and a Hired Gun from the Sirocco, who have followed the same trail one step behind, arriving up the outside stair while the party is talking to Vivian
secrets: CLUE C4c (core, any of three routes): Bunny Shearer, Percy Ainsworth or Agnes Whitlow, asked who Vivian's friends were before she was famous, will name Mags Fennimore 'who lives over the merry-go-round at the beach'.

Ambler's men found the pier the same way the party did, through Mrs. Sloane's frightened neighbour or by following the party's car from Bunker Hill (if the party did not check for a tail; Perception DC 14 on the drive spots a tan Chevrolet). If the party was careful and fast, they arrive half an hour ahead of Tiny; if not, Tiny is already on the stairs.

Vivian does not have the ledger in the apartment. It is in the carousel, inside the hollow body of the outside-row black horse with the gold mane, the one Mags rode in a picture in 1919. Only Mags and Vivian know. She will not give it up in this scenario.

synopsis: Harlan Shay, the studio fixer at Castellane Pictures, hires the party to find Vivian Lark, a contract actress missing for nine days, before the newspapers or the committee's investigators notice. He says she ran off with a man. The clues say otherwise: she left the studio's furs and took her mother's photograph; she had the studio driver Bunny Shearer take her to Union Station, bought a ticket to Bakersfield and did not get on; she went back to the Bunker Hill rooming house where she lived as Dorothy Pell before she was a star, until a very large man from Club Sirocco knocked her landlady into a door frame. Her friend, the screenwriter Abel Kurland, freshly served with a committee subpoena, charms the party and lies to them; his answering service has a Santa Monica number. The trail ends in the fog at the Santa Monica pier, in an apartment above the carousel, where Vivian tells the party a part of the truth (she took something from the Sirocco that proves someone bought the city council, and a councilman who would not be bought is dead) just before Royce Ambler's men come up the stairs. She will not go back to the studio and she asks the party one thing: Abel isn't answering his phone; go and see that he is all right. At dawn on Wednesday they find him at the bottom of his own pool.
hook: Harlan Shay's five hundred dollars is in fifties, crisp from the bank. The portrait he slides across the desk is the kind the studio sends to fan magazines: a dark-haired girl with a wide mouth and serious eyes, looking slightly past the camera as if somebody behind it has just said something she doesn't believe. 'Vivian Lark,' he says. 'Twenty-four. Seven pictures, the last one her first lead. She walked off the lot on Saturday the thirteenth and hasn't come back. No note. No calls. I've told the press she's resting in Palm Springs, and I can tell them that for about another week.' Outside the window a man walks past carrying a stuffed bear for somebody's picture. 'She's a good kid from a small town. Somebody has turned her head. I want to know where she is. I don't want her frightened, I don't want the police, and I don't want to read about it. Report to me every night at nine.' He looks at each of you in turn and smiles very kindly. 'And if anybody from Washington asks you anything at all, you've never heard of us.'

conclusions.conclusion: Vivian left on her own and is hiding. She was not kidnapped, she is not dead, and she did not run off with a man.
clues: C1a: Her dressing bungalow: her own things gone, the studio's left behind (Castellane lot)
C1b: The transport log, Car 11, Shearer, Union Station, Sunday 9:15 p.m.; or Bunny Shearer herself (Castellane lot)
C1c: The unused Bakersfield ticket and the redcap who saw her walk out to the streetcars (Union Station)
C1d (bonus): Percy Ainsworth, as her agent, can find out that she withdrew all $1,140 of her savings in cash on Friday 12 September (she banks at the Hollywood office of Pacific Union Trust)

conclusions.conclusion: She is living under her birth name, Dorothy 'Dot' Pell, on Bunker Hill.
clues: C2a: Her personnel card, or Percy, gives her legal name and old address (Castellane lot)
C2b: Mrs. Sloane's postcard in the wastebasket (Castellane lot)
C2c: Locker 212 rented in the name D. Pell (Union Station)
C2d: The Angels Flight operator's 'Dot' every morning (Bunker Hill)

conclusions.conclusion: She took something from Club Sirocco, and Royce Ambler's men are hunting her for it.
clues: C3a: Tiny Bascombe's visit and Mrs. Sloane's bruise (Bunker Hill)
C3b: Kurland's fear and the Sirocco menu with initials on his corkboard (Laurel Canyon)
C3c: Ambler has telephoned Percy Ainsworth three times offering to forgive his $3,000 in card markers if Percy finds out 'whether Vivian has anything of mine' (Percy's office or Percy's player)
C3d: The hat-check girl's account of the thirteenth and the safe man from Glendale (Club Sirocco)

conclusions.conclusion: She is in Mags Fennimore's apartment above the Santa Monica carousel.
clues: C4a: The Playland photo-booth strip in room 9, and Mrs. Sloane naming Mags (Bunker Hill)
C4b: Kurland's answering service and the Hippodrome Building number (Laurel Canyon)
C4c: Bunny, Percy or Agnes naming Mags as Vivian's first landlady 'over the merry-go-round' (any)

acts.title: Act 1: The Castle
acts.description: Monday 22 September. The hiring, the studio, and the first trail. Establish Harlan Shay as charming, generous and evasive, the lot as a factory of make-believe with its own police, and Vivian as a person the players start to like before they meet her. Plant the Nightly Report rule early: Shay wants a call every evening at nine.
objectives: Take Shay's job (and his $500) and learn what he is willing to say
Find her legal name and old address
Learn from the transport log, or from Bunny, that she was driven to Union Station
Meet Agnes Whitlow, Percy Ainsworth's world, and the studio's gossip

scenes.name: The Bungalow with the Lemon Tree
scenes.description: Harlan Shay's briefing. He is warm, quick, a little tired, and lies smoothly about why Vivian left. He has three telephones and answers none of them while the party is there.
scenes.readAloud: The bungalow is cool after the heat outside, all white walls and green leather and a ceiling fan that turns as slowly as a man thinking. There are no photographs of stars on the walls, only one framed thing: a cheque for one dollar, made out to Harlan Shay in 1927 and signed by Bernard Castellane, never cashed. Shay sees you looking at it. 'My first fee,' he says. 'He told me I'd be paid what I was worth. I've been trying to collect ever since.' He pours coffee from a silver pot without asking how you take it, and gets it right.

skillChecks.success: Shay does not believe his own story about a man. He is frightened, and not for Vivian: for something she knows or has. When he says 'the gentlemen from Washington', his hand tightens on the cup.
skillChecks.failure: Shay seems exactly what he says he is: a decent man protecting a studio's investment and a young woman's reputation.

skillChecks.success: You know Shay's reputation: twenty years as Castellane's fixer, the man who made a star's drunk-driving accident into a heroic swerve to avoid a child, who paid off a starlet's husband in 1938 and got the husband a job in Mexico. He is said to never carry a gun and never forget a name.
skillChecks.failure: You know he is important at the studio and that is all.

scenes.name: Vivian's Dressing Bungalow
scenes.description: The bungalow is the first core clue: the shape of what she took and what she left. Agnes Whitlow may turn up with a script under her arm to see who is going through Vivian's things.
scenes.readAloud: The name board by the door says VIVIAN LARK in neat white paint over a darker patch where another name used to be. Inside it smells of cold cream and dust. There is a daybed with a crocheted throw, a dressing table under a ring of bare bulbs, and a rack of gowns in cellophane, each with a wardrobe department tag. A mink stole hangs by itself on a padded hanger like someone was careful with it. The mirror frame has the little bare marks where photographs used to be tucked, and only one is left: a publicity still of a horse.

skillChecks.success: Bonus detail: the gowns are the studio's; the cotton dresses the wardrobe girls say she wore on the lot are gone; the makeup case on the dressing table is the studio's, but the little tin box she kept her own lipstick and her mother's ring in is missing. She packed light and she packed what was hers. (C1a is core; this roll adds the inventory.)
skillChecks.failure: It is a room someone left. You note it was left tidy, and that the studio's things are all here.

skillChecks.success: In the wastebasket under some blotted tissues: a torn Angels Flight postcard from 'G. Sloane, Alta Vista Rooms' (C2b, core, found on any search of the basket) and a Sirocco matchbook with '4-17' pencilled inside the flap.
skillChecks.failure: You find the postcard (core) but miss the matchbook, which Agnes Whitlow later picks out of the basket and hands to you without a word.

scenes.name: The Transport Garage
scenes.description: Studio cars and the dispatcher, Morrie Kaplan, a big friendly man who keeps a perfect log and a racing form. If Bunny Shearer is in the party, this is her scene: her player decides when, and whether, to say she drove Vivian to Union Station.
scenes.readAloud: The transport garage is a cathedral of black Cadillacs and wood-sided station wagons, and it smells of wax and gasoline. A radio on a shelf is giving the race results from Del Mar. Behind a window with a brass grille sits a large man in a cardigan with a ledger the size of a family Bible, which he opens for you, turning it round with two fingers as if it were holy.

skillChecks.success: Morrie shows you the log (C1b, core): Car 11, Shearer, out 9:15 p.m. Sunday 14 September, destination Union Sta., in 10:30. 'Bunny took Miss Lark somewhere that night,' he says. 'Bunny don't talk about passengers. That's why they like her.'
skillChecks.failure: Morrie wants to know who's asking and calls Shay's bungalow; Shay says to give them anything they want, and Morrie does, a little stiffly. Shay now knows exactly what the party looked at.

encounters: No combat is expected in this act. The studio police will escort out anyone caught breaking into offices; that is +1 Heat and a call to Shay.
Agnes Whitlow (companion), who can join the party from here if they treat her as a colleague and not a secretary

acts.title: Act 2: Dot Pell
acts.description: Monday afternoon to Tuesday evening. Union Station, Bunker Hill, Laurel Canyon and perhaps the Sirocco, in whatever order the party chooses. Every location points to at least two others. The party learns she was not taken, that she is living as Dot Pell, that the Sirocco is hunting her, and where she has gone. The Tuesday visit to Abel Kurland is the hinge of the campaign: play him warmly so his death lands.
objectives: Find the unused ticket and locker 212 at Union Station
Find the Alta Vista Rooms and earn Mrs. Sloane's trust
Learn that Tiny Bascombe and the Sirocco are hunting her
Talk to Abel Kurland and read what he will not say
Decide what to tell Harlan Shay at nine o'clock

scenes.name: The Waiting Room
scenes.description: Union Station. The ticket clerk's book, locker 212, and Clarence Webb on the redcaps' bench.
scenes.readAloud: Union Station is cool and enormous and hushed, like a church that sells tickets. Sunlight comes down through high windows onto the leather armchairs, where soldiers sleep with their caps over their faces and a family with eleven suitcases waits for the Sunset Limited. On the north patio a row of redcaps sit on a bench in the shade of a pepper tree, and the oldest of them watches you come with the patience of a man who has seen everyone in Los Angeles arrive at least once.

skillChecks.success: The ticket clerk looks up the Sunday sales (C1c, core): one coach to Bakersfield, 'Miss V. Lark', 9:52 p.m., and the conductor's count was one short. With success, she adds that the lady asked for a seat by the window and seemed to be crying.
skillChecks.failure: The clerk shows you the stub (core) but will not say anything else without a supervisor.

skillChecks.success: Locker 212 opens without the claim check and without anyone looking. (With Bunny's claim check, no roll; or $5 to the left-luggage man.) Inside: the white fox, the paste necklace, two gowns. C2c, core: the left-luggage card says 'D. Pell'.
skillChecks.failure: A Beat Cop sees you working on a locker. Talk your way out (Deception DC 12) or +1 Heat and a trip to the station office, where a call to the studio gets you released and tells Shay where you are.

scenes.name: Angels Flight
scenes.description: Up the funicular to Clay Street, the Alta Vista Rooms, Mrs. Sloane's bruise and room 9.
scenes.readAloud: The little orange car is called Olivet and it climbs the hill at an angle that puts your back against the bench, clanking, past the backs of buildings and laundry lines and a cat asleep on a fire escape, while its twin, Sinai, slides down past you on the other rail. At the top the operator takes your penny without looking up from his book. The Alta Vista is half a block on: a turreted wooden mansion gone the grey of old teeth, with geraniums in coffee cans on the porch and a hand-lettered sign that says ROOMS BY THE WEEK, NO DRINKING, NO PETS, NO ACTORS. Someone has crossed out NO ACTORS and written, in a different hand, EXCEPT ONE.

skillChecks.success: Mrs. Sloane decides you are kind. She tells you about Tiny Bascombe and her teacup (C3a, core, which she will tell anyone who is not threatening), about Dot leaving on Saturday night, and gives you Dot's message: she's all right and she'll pay her back. She lets you see room 9.
skillChecks.failure: Mrs. Sloane tells you about the big man who hurt her (core) but will not let you upstairs. Room 9 has a window over the porch roof (Athletics DC 12, +1 Heat if seen) or Mrs. Sloane's trombonist lodger can be persuaded for a dollar.

skillChecks.success: Room 9: C4a, core, the photo-booth strip in the mirror frame. Bonus: a notebook page with lines from The Gilded Hour written out by hand and, underneath, in the same hand: 'Abel has the rest. Abel will know what to do.'
skillChecks.failure: You find the photo strip (core). The notebook page you find only if Mrs. Sloane shows you.

skillChecks.success: Bunker Hill talks. The shoeshine man on Hill Street says the big man in the camel coat drives a black '41 Buick and has been back twice, the last time with two younger men who looked like they'd been told to break something.
skillChecks.failure: Nobody on the hill wants to talk to strangers about men who break teacups.

scenes.name: A Writer at Home
scenes.description: Tuesday afternoon in Laurel Canyon. Abel Kurland, with a subpoena on the desk he has not opened, gin he has not drunk, and a script he will not stop working on. He is the most likeable man in the scenario and he lies to protect Vivian. Play him as a man who thinks he has a plan.
scenes.readAloud: Kurland opens the door himself in shirtsleeves, horn-rimmed glasses pushed up on his forehead, a pencil behind his ear and another in his mouth. He takes the pencil out to speak. 'You're not from the committee,' he says, 'they come in pairs and they don't smile. You're not from the studio, they telephone first. So you must be from Harlan, who does neither.' He steps back to let you in. The study beyond is a landslide of books. On the desk, under a coffee cup, is a long envelope with a congressional seal, unopened. 'Don't mind that,' he says. 'It's an invitation to Washington. I haven't decided what to wear.'

skillChecks.success: C3b, core, is that he flinches at the Sirocco; on a success you also see that he knows exactly where Vivian is, that he is not afraid of the subpoena so much as angry, and that he has the look of a man holding a winning hand who is not sure he will be allowed to play it.
skillChecks.failure: He flinches at the Sirocco (core) and otherwise he is a funny, tired man with a subpoena who has no idea where Vivian is. He is a professional; he writes liars for a living.

skillChecks.success: The Sirocco card-room menu on his corkboard, with initials on the back (C3b detail), and the answering-service number taped to the phone (the route to C4b).
skillChecks.failure: His corkboard is index cards for a screenplay called Dry Wells and you do not look closer.

skillChecks.success: Honesty works on him. If the party admits who hired them and says they will not take Vivian back against her will, he says: 'Then here's a thing for free. Don't tell Harlan you've been here. Don't tell Harlan anything. He's a decent man, and decent men do whatever they're paid for.' He will not say where she is.
skillChecks.failure: 'Tell Harlan she's in Mexico,' he says, and shows you out with a joke.

scenes.name: Nine O'Clock
scenes.description: The nightly telephone report to Shay. Play it as a scene, not a formality. Shay is sympathetic, thanks them, asks gentle questions about Kurland. Whatever they say about Kurland, Shay drives to Laurel Canyon at eleven. If the party does not call at all, he goes anyway, because Lyle Preston told him at dinner that Kurland had boasted of 'insurance'.
scenes.readAloud: The payphone is in a drugstore on Sunset that smells of malted milk and iodine. You give the operator the studio number and extension seven, and Shay picks up on the first ring, as if he has been sitting with his hand on the receiver. 'Tell me everything,' he says pleasantly. Behind his voice you can hear a radio playing dance music very softly, and ice in a glass.

skillChecks.success: When Kurland's name comes up, Shay goes quiet for a second too long, and then asks whether Kurland was 'alone up there'. Remember this tomorrow.
skillChecks.failure: Shay is grateful, and tells you to get some sleep.

encounters: A Pickpocket at Union Station (CR 0); a Beat Cop if lockers are forced
Two Street Toughs from the Sirocco on Bunker Hill if the party arrives after Tuesday noon

Royce Ambler, Tiny Bascombe and a Bouncer at Club Sirocco if the party goes there; no fight unless the party starts one, in which case the Sheriff's deputies arrive in five minutes and know whose side they're on (+2 Heat)

acts.title: Act 3: The Carousel
acts.description: Tuesday night 23 September into Wednesday dawn. The party reaches the Santa Monica pier in the fog, finds Mags Fennimore and Vivian, hears part of the truth, and fights Ambler's men on the stairs, the carousel floor and the pier. Vivian asks them to check on Abel. At dawn, in Laurel Canyon, they find him in the pool.
objectives: Reach the pier, ideally without being followed
Win Mags Fennimore's trust and talk to Vivian
Learn what Vivian will tell them: she took proof from the Sirocco that someone has bought the council, and Councilman Mabry died for refusing
Protect Vivian from Tiny Bascombe and his men
Decide where Vivian goes now, and what to tell Shay
Go to Laurel Canyon at dawn

scenes.name: Over the Merry-Go-Round
scenes.description: The Hippodrome after closing: the carousel lights off, the fog in, the foghorn every thirty seconds. Mags meets the party at her door with a carving knife. Vivian is behind her.
scenes.readAloud: The pier is a road of wet planks going out into nothing. The fog has eaten the sea and the town behind you and left only what is close: a bait-shop sign, a coil of rope, a fishing line going down through the rail into the white, the round bulk of the Hippodrome with its little towers and its dark windows. Somewhere out in the fog the horn groans, and the planks hum under your feet. The outside stair creaks. At the top a door opens before you can knock, and a tiny old woman in a silk kimono with white hair piled up like a meringue stands in it holding a carving knife the way a heroine holds a rose in a picture you have never seen. 'If you are from Mr. Ambler,' she says in a voice that was made to reach the back of a theatre with no microphone, 'you will find I am a great deal more trouble than I look.' Behind her, in the lamplight, a young woman in a man's cardigan is standing very still, and you know her face from a studio portrait.

skillChecks.success: Mags lowers the knife and puts the kettle on. Vivian sits down across from you and talks, and decides to trust one of you in particular (the one who was most honest; the GM chooses).
skillChecks.failure: Mags keeps the knife. Vivian talks anyway, standing up by the window, ready to run.

skillChecks.success: Vivian is telling the truth about what she saw and what she took. She is not telling you where it is, or what she means to do with it, and she is braver than she is frightened, but not by much.
skillChecks.failure: She is an actress. You cannot tell which parts are performance. Possibly she can't either.

scenes.name: What Vivian Says
scenes.description: Vivian's account, for the GM to deliver. She gives this much and no more in this scenario.
scenes.readAloud: 'Harlan sends some of us girls to the Sirocco to have dinner with men who are important to the studio. Dinner and dancing and laugh at their jokes. That's all, mostly. On the thirteenth I went upstairs to find my wrap and I heard Royce Ambler and a man I didn't know in the corridor. The other man said, Mabry's taken care of, and the next one will be too if he won't play. Arthur Mabry is the councilman who drove off Mulholland three weeks ago. It was in the papers. An accident.' She turns her cup round in its saucer. 'I've watched Royce open that safe twenty times. He uses his birthday. So I opened it. There's a book in there with every dollar and every name, and photographs. I took them. I gave half to someone who knows what to do with them, and I've got the other half where nobody will find it. I'm not going back to Harlan. He sent me there.' She looks up. 'Abel isn't answering his phone. He always answers his phone. Will you go and see?'

skillChecks.success: She tells you the other man in the corridor was 'big, sixty, a pink face, a ring with a blue stone, he talked about acres', which Percy, Agnes or any Society check DC 13 can name as Wendell Haig, the Valley real-estate man.
skillChecks.failure: 'I didn't know him,' she says, and that is all.

scenes.name: The Stairs
scenes.description: Tiny Bascombe, two Street Toughs and a Hired Gun come up the outside stair and the inside stair at once. They want Vivian alive and the book. The fight runs through Mags's apartment, down onto the dark carousel floor among the horses (anyone can throw the switch: the carousel starts turning and the band organ plays, and fighting on it is difficult terrain with cover behind the horses), and out onto the foggy pier. Mags fights with a carving knife and astonishing language.
scenes.readAloud: The foghorn sounds, and in the silence after it you hear the outside stair creak under something very heavy. Then the inside stair creaks too. Mags puts down her teacup. 'Well,' she says, 'I always did prefer a big finish.'

skillChecks.success: You hear both stairs. Nobody is surprised, and the party can choose where to stand.
skillChecks.failure: Only the outside stair; the men on the inside stair have surprise in the first round.

skillChecks.success: You find the carousel's switch in the operator's booth and throw it. Lights blaze, the band organ bursts into 'Over the Waves', the horses rise and fall, and every attacker on the floor has disadvantage on ranged attacks for a round while their eyes adjust.
skillChecks.failure: The switch sticks; the lights flicker and die. It works on the next try.

skillChecks.success: With two of them down, Tiny's nerve goes. He drags his men off down the pier into the fog, promising that Mr. Ambler will remember this.
skillChecks.failure: They fight until two are down, then run anyway.

scenes.name: Lookout Mountain, Dawn
scenes.description: The party drives Vivian (or leaves her with Mags, or with Dr. Pryor on Central Avenue) and goes up to Laurel Canyon in the first grey light. The house is open. The pool light is still on. Abel Kurland is at the bottom of the deep end in his shirtsleeves. End the scenario here.
scenes.readAloud: The canyon is cold at this hour and smells of sage and eucalyptus, and somewhere a rooster on a hillside thinks it lives in the country. Kurland's front door is open a hand's width. Nobody answers. The living room lamps are on. Through the wall of glass the pool glows a soft impossible blue in the grey morning, lit from below, very still. At the bottom of the deep end, his shirt pale and ballooned, one arm drifting as if he were waving at something far away, is Abel Kurland.

skillChecks.success: Before you touch anything: there is an empty gin bottle on the deck by the diving board, a dark stain on the coping at the deep end, and his reading glasses on the bottom of the pool, a long way from his body. (These are the first K1 clues for kl-scenario-002.)
skillChecks.failure: A dead man in a pool, an empty bottle. It looks exactly like what it is meant to look like.

encounters: Tiny Bascombe (use Bouncer, with 22 hit points and a sap: Blackjack 1d4+2), two Street Toughs and one Hired Gun (.38 revolver); they want Vivian alive and will not shoot at her; they break off when two are down or the pier's night watchman fires his shotgun in the air
A Night Watchman on the pier who calls the Santa Monica police if there is gunfire; they arrive in eight minutes (+3 Heat for gunfire, +2 for a body)
Mags Fennimore (non-combatant who refuses to be one) and Vivian Lark (companion)

npcsInvolved.name: Harlan Shay, 52
npcsInvolved.role: The client; Castellane Pictures' fixer; secretly the man who will let Abel Kurland drown tonight
npcsInvolved.description: Silver-haired, soft-spoken, beautifully dressed, never carries a gun, never forgets a name or a birthday, solves problems with money and has done for twenty years. Kind to waiters. Pays well, on time, in cash. He should be the most reassuring person in the scenario.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get the ledger and the negatives back before anyone sees them, because one of the photographs shows him handing a councilman an envelope. Protect the studio, which is the only thing he has ever been loyal to. He tells himself he wants Vivian safe, and partly he does.

npcsInvolved.name: Vivian Lark (Dorothy Ann Pell), 24
npcsInvolved.role: The missing actress; companion from the end of this scenario
npcsInvolved.description: From Taft, California, an oil town where her father died in a derrick fire. Came to Los Angeles at eighteen, boarded with Mags Fennimore, sang in clubs, was signed by Castellane at twenty. Funny, sharp, guarded, braver than she looks. Full sheet in the companion files.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To finish Haig and Ambler herself, in public, under her own name, and to stop being something men hand each other across a table.

npcsInvolved.name: Abel Kurland, 44
npcsInvolved.role: Screenwriter, Vivian's friend; dies on Tuesday night
npcsInvolved.description: Ex-newspaperman (he was Roz Keane's first city editor at the Evening Courier), witty, rumpled, generous, a little vain, the best writer on the Castellane lot. Went to some meetings in 1938 and has a subpoena on his desk because of it. He has the negatives hidden and a plan to use them.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To trade the negatives to Bernard Castellane for two things: the studio gives the committee no names, and the West Valley vote dies. He thinks he can do it quietly. He is wrong.

npcsInvolved.name: Royce Ambler, 49
npcsInvolved.role: Owner of Club Sirocco on the Sunset Strip
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, courteous, grey at the temples, a Kansas City accent and a Kansas City past in the liquor trade. Polite to everyone, frightened of only one man, Wendell Haig, who does not yet know the ledger is gone.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Get the book and the negatives back before Haig finds out they are missing. Failing that, sell Haig to whoever will pay and keep himself alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Tiny Bascombe
npcsInvolved.description: Six foot six, camel overcoat in all weathers, soft voice, hands like shovels, a Sirocco doorman's pin. He hurt Mrs. Sloane and is privately ashamed of it.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Do what Mr. Ambler says and not think about it.

npcsInvolved.name: Mrs. Gertrude 'Gertie' Sloane, 70
npcsInvolved.role: Landlady of the Alta Vista Rooms, Bunker Hill
npcsInvolved.description: Widow of a Santa Fe railroad conductor, ferns, glued teacups, a bruise, a sharp tongue and a soft heart. Loves Dot like a granddaughter.
npcsInvolved.motivation: That Dot is safe, and that the big man never comes back.

npcsInvolved.name: Marguerite 'Mags' Fennimore, 72
npcsInvolved.role: Retired silent-picture actress; Vivian's first landlady; lives above the Santa Monica carousel
npcsInvolved.description: Tiny, white-haired, enormous eyes, silk kimonos, a voice built for a theatre with no microphone, and opinions about everyone in Hollywood since 1912. Reads the fortune cards at the arcade for a living.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To have one more good scene, and to keep her girl alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Agnes Whitlow, 54
npcsInvolved.role: Script supervisor on The Gilded Hour; companion
npcsInvolved.description: Full sheet in the companion files. Notices everything, remembers everything, and has been ignored by producers for twenty-five years, which has made her the best-informed woman on the lot.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To find out what happened to the girl who once asked her, sincerely, how she kept track of everything.

npcsInvolved.name: Clarence Webb, Albert Dunphy and Dolores 'Dee Dee' Carmody
npcsInvolved.role: Witnesses: the Union Station redcap, the Angels Flight operator, the Sirocco hat-check girl
npcsInvolved.description: Working people who see everything because nobody looks at them. Each will help a polite party for a dollar and help a kind one for nothing.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Respect, a tip, and not to be dragged into anything.

rewards.money: Shay's $500 retainer (split it among the party: add the shares to wallet lines) and $50 a day each while they keep reporting; Tiny's men carry $40 between them; Mags gives nothing and offers a fortune reading for free.
items: The Sirocco matchbook with '4-17' inside the flap
The contents of locker 212: a white fox fur, a paste necklace and two gowns (studio property; worth $600 to a fence, worth goodwill if returned to wardrobe)
Mrs. Sloane's postcard and the photo-booth strip
A .38 revolver from the Hired Gun, if beaten, and .38 rounds (12)
Vivian Lark, as a companion, if the party has earned her trust
Clues C1 to C4, and the first look at the K1 clues in Kurland's pool

twists: The client is lying. Shay knows exactly why Vivian ran, and he wants what she took more than he wants her. Nothing in this scenario proves it; Insight at the briefing and his question 'was he alone up there' on the telephone are honest, early hints.

Vivian is not a victim. She planned her disappearance well enough to fool a studio: a false trail to Bakersfield, the studio's furs left as a message, her own name as a disguise. Let the players admire it.

The nightly report kills Abel Kurland. Whatever the party tells Shay on Tuesday evening, Shay drives to Laurel Canyon at eleven. If the party told him nothing, he went anyway, on Lyle Preston's gossip. The players should eventually work out that their report may have sent the killer; it should haunt them, not paralyze them, and the GM should be clear afterwards that Shay would have gone regardless.

Royce Ambler and Harlan Shay are hunting the same thing for different masters, and neither knows how much the other knows. Two hunters on one trail: the party may find Ambler's men one step behind them, or Shay's studio police one step ahead, and can play them against each other.
The ledger is inside a carousel horse. Nobody will find it in this scenario, and that is right: Vivian keeps it until she decides who has earned it.
dmTips: This is a legwork scenario. Budget the time: Act 1 about an hour, Act 2 the main event (two hours, played as a sandbox), Act 3 a sharp, loud ending and a quiet last image. The only expected fight is on the pier.

Core clues are automatic. If the party searches the bungalow, they find the postcard; if they ask the ticket clerk, they get the unused ticket. Rolls add detail and speed. If the players are stuck on Tuesday afternoon, have Agnes or Percy remember Mags Fennimore, and run the case board.

Play Shay warmly and generously. He should be the person the players most want to please. He pays on time, remembers their names, asks after their families. The betrayal in kl-scenario-002 depends on this.

Play Kurland's scene as a gift. He is funny and brave and he lies well. Give him one good line about the committee ('They want me to tell them who I had dinner with in 1938. I'd love to know myself. I was very drunk in 1938.') and one about Vivian ('She is the only person on this lot who reads the whole script'). The players should want to see him again.

Track what Shay knows in the world state. Every nightly report is information he acts on. If the party mentions Bunker Hill on Monday night, studio police are at the Alta Vista on Tuesday morning asking politely, which Mrs. Sloane will mention.
Bunny Shearer's secret (she drove Vivian to Union Station and has a sealed envelope with the locker claim check) belongs to her player. Do not force it out; let the transport log make it awkward.
Level-up note: the 600 XP in this file is per character and takes each character from 2nd to 3rd level. Award it at the pool at dawn.

Period texture: the Dodgers in the pennant race on the radio, a newsboy shouting about subpoenas, nylons in a shop window, a Red Car clanging past on Santa Monica Boulevard, a veteran in an Ike jacket selling apples, the carousel's band organ playing 'Over the Waves'.
